question: Apply the four pillars of Object-Oriented Programming in designing a real-world application. Explain each concept with suitable examples.
answer:
1. Introduction                                           (1 Mark)
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) organizes software around objects and classes.
The four pillars of OOP are:
Abstraction
Encapsulation
Inheritance
Polymorphism
These concepts improve modularity, reusability, flexibility, and maintainability.
2. Abstraction                                           (3 Marks)
Hides implementation details and exposes only essential features.
Focuses on what an object does, not how it does it.
Implemented using abstract classes or interfaces.
Car: A driver uses the accelerator, brake, and steering without knowing the internal engine mechanism.
3. Encapsulation                                       (3 Marks)
Combines data and methods into a single class.
Restricts direct access to data using access modifiers.
Uses private data members and public getter/setter methods.
TV Remote Control: Users operate the TV without accessing internal electronic circuits.
4. Inheritance                                            (3 Marks)
A subclass acquires the properties and methods of a superclass.
Establishes an "is-a" relationship.
Uses the extends keyword in Java.
Vehicle → Car
Employee → Programmer / Manager
5. Polymorphism (3 Marks)
One interface, many implementations.
The same method behaves differently depending on the object.
Method Overloading-Compile-time Polymorphism
Method Overriding -Run-time Polymorphism
Shape.draw() displays different outputs for Circle, Rectangle, and Triangle.

question: Analyze how Garbage Collection contributes to efficient memory management in Java applications. Develop a suitable Java program and justify its impact on application reliability and resource utilization.
answer:
Garbage Collection:                                 (2 Marks)
Garbage Collection (GC) is an automatic memory management process performed by the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).
It removes unreachable (unused) objects from heap memory, preventing memory leaks.
Working of Garbage Collection              (4 Marks)
Objects are created in Heap Memory.
JVM identifies reachable and unreachable objects.
GC Roots include:
Local variables , Active threads ,Static variables, JNI references
Mark Phase: Marks reachable objects.
Sweep Phase: Removes unreachable objects.
Compact Phase: Rearranges memory to reduce fragmentation.
Generational Garbage Collection:
Young Generation ,Old Generation ,Most newly created objects are short-lived.
Impact                                                      (2 Marks)
Reliability
Prevents memory leaks.
Reduces programmer errors due to manual memory management.
Improves application stability.
Resource Utilization
Frees unused heap memory.
Improves memory efficiency.
Optimizes application performance.
Program                                                   (5 Marks)
Class
class Demo {
protected void finalize() {
System.out.println("Object is garbage collected");
}   }
Object Creation
Demo obj = new Demo();
Eligible for GC
obj = null;
Request Garbage Collection
System.gc();

Therefore, the overridden sound() method in Dog is executed at runtime.

answer:
1. Thread Life Cycle                               (3 Marks)
New – Thread object is created.
Runnable – start() is called; thread is ready to execute.
Running – CPU executes the thread.
Blocked / Waiting / Timed Waiting – Thread waits for a resource, notification, or specified time.
Terminated (Dead) – Execution of run() method is completed.
JVM scheduler controls movement between Runnable and Running states.
2. Thread State Transition Diagram        (3 Marks)
3. Effect start(), sleep(), wait(), join()  (3 Marks)
start()
Creates a new thread.
Moves thread from New → Runnable.
sleep()
Suspends execution for a specified time.
Moves Running → Timed Waiting.
wait()
Releases the object's lock.
Moves thread to Waiting state until notify() or notifyAll() is called.
join()
Causes the calling thread to wait until another thread completes.
4. Java Program                                        (4 Marks)
MyThread t = new MyThread();
t.start();
Thread.sleep(1000);
t.join();
t.getState();
